خِلَالٌ A thing with which one perforates, or transpierces, a thing, (JK, K,) either of iron or of wood: (JK:) pl. أَخِلَّةٌ. (K.) ―
-b2- A wooden thing [or pin] (S, Msb,) with which one pins a garment, (T, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) conjoining its two edges: (Mgh, Msb:) pl. as above: (S, Msb:) which also signifies the small pieces of wood with which one pins together the edges of the oblong pieces of cloth of a tent. (TA.) ―
-b3- [A skewer for flesh-meat.] ―
-b4- A wooden pin which is inserted into the tongue of a young camel, in order that he may not such: (K:) or which is fixed above the nose of a young camel, for that purpose. (TA in art. لهج.) ―
-b5- [A toothpick;] a thing (of wood, S, Msb) with which one extracts the remains of food between his teeth; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ خِلَالَةٌ . (Har p. 101.) ―
-b6- [A long thorn or prickle: such being often used as a pin and as a toothpick.] ＝
-A2- See also خُلَالَةٌ. ＝
-A3- And see خَلَلٌ, in six places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
